body:
Hi, I dont understand V5.21 "Verify that applications have defined positive validation for all input fields, with permissible exceptions to allow characters that might otherwise be rejected." 

The first part is white-listing, right? The second part grey-listing? How would you do that?

comments.body:
This is indeed quite cryptic and should be reworder to say more clearly what is expected. "Positive validation" and "white-listing" are jargon. I would start with agreeing on what we want to achieve and then wording it in unambigous way:
- All input data should be validated _(not only "fields", as "fields" imply HTML forms, and input may come through REST calls, query parameters etc)_
- Structured data should be strictly validated against a defined schema including allowed characters, length and pattern _(e.g. a social security number or telephone)_
- Unstructured data should be sanitized to enforce generic safety measures such as allowed characters and length, and characters potentially harmful in given context should be removed or escaped _(e.g. natural names with Unicode or apostrophes, such as Këvïn or O'Hara)_
These are great suggestions to improve an old requirement. I will work on incorporating new text.

title: Q on V5.21: grey-listing?
